title: A fair price for a coin game?
hook: Flip until tails; the payout doubles with each flip. What should entry cost?

knows: an average payout is total winnings divided by plays
doesNotKnow: that an average can be made mostly of rare big payouts
that a typical player may never see it

misconception: A game with typical payouts of a few dollars cannot have a high fair price.
objective: The learner can say that the fair price is the long-run average payout ($20 here), that it comes from rare big wins, and that most plays pay $4 or less.
keyState: A price chosen and at least 200 games played; on the click path 550 games with average $25.79, median $4 and biggest $8,192 (58% of all winnings).

claims.text: The game: flip a fair coin until the first tails, at most 20 flips; first tails on flip k pays $2^k, and 20 heads pays $0.
claims.source: Rules shown on the stage and in the question; payout() in model.ts.

claims.text: Why $20? Tails first on flip 1 pays $2 half the time: $1 of the average. On flip 2, $4 a quarter of the time: $1. Every flip's fair share is $1, so 20 flips make $20 (each k from 1 to 20 adds 2^k x (1/2)^k = $1).
claims.source: Sum over k = 1..20 of 2^k (1/2)^k = 20 (fairPrice() in model.ts, recomputed in node). The probability of first tails on flip k is (1/2)^k. | v2 (2026-10-14): options parallel and payouts spelled out; reveal shows the $1-per-flip working; previous verification void, needs re-check. | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): Reveal now points at the new per-flip strip on stage; the 'flip 3, $8 an eighth' sentence was dropped for length. The old closing 'Another run could show a lower average' (c5) is no longer shown.
P(first tails on flip 1) + P(flip 2) = 1/2 + 1/4 = 3/4; payouts $2 and $4.

claims.text: In the stage's seeded run, the average payout after 550 games is $25.79, the median payout is $4 and the biggest payout is $8,192, which is 58% of all money paid out.
claims.source: Game g uses mulberry32(2500 + g), untuned (first seed tried). One early $8,192 payout lifts this run above the typical case: over 400 other seed sets of 550 games the average had median $11.6, 10th to 90th percentile $8.1 to $25.7 (min $6.2, max $969), and only 13.5% reached $20 or more.

claims.text: The running average can sit well below $20 for many games because the big payouts are rare, so a run is not a reliable guide to the fair price.
claims.source: Spread across seeds in claim 4: the median 550-game average is $11.6, below $20; the variance of one payout is the sum of 4^k (1/2)^k = about 2.1 million.

claims.text: The 'Your profit' readout is the player's profit: total payouts minus price times games played.
claims.source: profit = summary(n).total - price x n in Demo.tsx. | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): Label changed from 'Profit' to 'Your profit' (r5: a beginner may read it as the house's).

claims.text: Stage strip: 'your average split by the flip tails came on (fair share $1 each)': bar k is (games whose first tails was on flip k) x $2^k / games, so the 20 bars add up to the running average; a dashed line marks $1, bars above $2 are capped and labelled with their value.
claims.source: shares() in Demo.tsx. The bars sum to total payout / games = the average readout. The fair share of flip k is 2^k x (1/2)^k = $1 (c2). | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): new sentence. New stage element: shows the $1-per-flip cause (decision 2026-10-14-told-vs-shown).

claims.text: In your strip, flips 1 to m each gave about $1, flip K gave $X from N rare win(s) and E of the 20 never came up, so gave $0 (computed from the learner's own games; 'about $1' means between $0.50 and $1.60). Seeded run at 550 games: flips 1 to 9 about $1 (0.93 to 1.22), flip 13 $14.89 from 1 win, 9 flips never came up.
claims.source: readStrip() in Demo.tsx over the seeded games (model.ts, mulberry32(2500 + g)); builder's separate node re-run of seeds 2500-3049 gave the 550-game shares 0.99, 0.93, 1.12, 1.05, 1.22, 0.93, 0.93, 0.93, 0.93, 1.86, 0, 0, 14.89, 0 ... 0 (sum 25.79, matching c4). | REVISED v3 2026-10-14 (demo-builder, wave D r5): new sentence. New reveal sentence.

recall.question: A game pays $1 million with chance 1 in 1,000 and nothing otherwise. Is $1,000 a fair entry price?
options: No, it must cost less than $1
recall.why: Fair price equals the average payout: 1/1000 x $1,000,000 = $1,000. Most plays pay nothing, but the rare big wins carry the average.
